sections.text: Introduction

Historical 
data for this document:

This document 
created from the document no. TD-SS-003-r0 by dividing it to 2 documents:

First as MPIS 
technical procedures document number T-001-r2 to illustrate how to take a sample 
of oil from equipment as transformer.

Second as MPIS 
technical directives document number: TD-SS-009-r0 to illustrate the insulating oil 
guidelines for test program.
Information

Frequency of testing: Once annually or more frequently as may be 
recommended by Central Chemical Labs.
Directives
Standard
Recommended acceptable results for gas in oil analysis are as follows:

Principal combustible gases generated in transformer oil and their causes are
shown in the Table below.
Carbon Monoxide, Carbon Dioxide
Recommended Guideline for Individual Gasses

As a guide, acceptable level of individual combustible gases in oil, the
Authority has adopted standards set by the IEC.
Maximum Value in PPM
Guideline for Total Dissolved Gas

The total ppm of all gases dissolved in oil should not exceed 700. Higher totals indicate incipient problems that require
specialized diagnosis.
Rate of Accumulation

In addition to guide lines listed above, the rate of gas generation also
provides critical information about changes occurring in the transformer. Rapid
build up indicates internal problems.
Monitoring of Dissolved Gas Levels

It is necessary to establish a computerized data base as a means of
monitoring the absolute levels and rate of increase of dissolved gases. Rigorous
monitoring will provide sample warning of incipient faults.

Guidelines for 
Gas Analysis Interpretation

Analysis of combustible 
gas provides a breakdown of the composition of the gas. These guides indicate 
probable location and type of fault.
Note:

In every case there may be other factors or variables that may alter the
interpretation.

In the interpretation of gas analysis information, three considerations are
crucial:

items: The total amount of combustible gas
The amount of each individual gas
The rate of increase of combustible gases.

sections.text: Acceptable Results for Basic Oil Tests

items:
Acceptable level is equal to or less than 0.4 mg (KOH) per gram of insulating
oil.

If neutralization number is between 0.4 and 0.7 then reclaim using filler
earth and vacuum treatment or completely replace oil, whichever is more
economical.
If level is more than 0.7 then replace oil.

Oil dielectric strength is good, if it is equal to or greater than 40 kv (by IEC 
 and VDE standard mm gap).

Minimum level for treatment is 25 kv by 
 (IEC and VDE standards).
Replace oil if dielectric strength is less than 25 kv
Minimum acceptable for new oil is 40 dynes/cm

Minimum level of IFT for treatment is 17
 dynes/cm
Replace oil if IFT < 15 dynes/cm or less.

A moisture level of 10 ppm or
less is acceptable.

If moisture level is more than 15
 ppm
then treat oil.
